title: Read without copying
description:
Write `int countSpaces(const std::string& text)` that returns how many space characters are in the text.

The parameter is a **const reference**: the function reads the caller's string directly (no copy, which matters when the text is long) and promises not to change it.
hints:
Loop over the indexes as in lesson 3.03, `for (std::size_t i{ 0 }; i < text.length(); ++i)`, and look at `text[i]`. Count the ones equal to `' '` (a space in single quotes: a `char`, not a string).

There is also a shorter loop that visits every character in turn, which lesson 5.01 covers properly: `for (char c : text) { ... }`.
